findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or unmatched
findings.body: The data migration reads the old embed_category setting with execute(...)[0]['id'] and, only if that id is 0, does the same for uncategorized_category_id. Site settings at their default are often not stored, and embed_category was a free-text category name, so the join on categories.name commonly returns no row. [0] is then nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError before the category_id == 0 fallback. The same crash happens on the uncategorized lookup if that row is missing. Because this runs in the up migration that also deletes those settings, a typical upgrade aborts and never creates embeddable_hosts, while the new code no longer reads SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts. Handle an empty result and fall back to a real category id before inserting rows.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unquoted
findings.body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)", bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalizer. The previous allow-list accepted http:// and https:// prefixes and paths (the old matcher used URI#host), but record_for_host compares only URI#host to the stored string. After upgrade, a saved value such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 will not match a referer host of discourse.org or example.com, so previously working embeds start returning invalid referer. A host containing a single quote also breaks the SQL or injects statements. Normalize (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and downcase) and insert with bound parameters. Windows newlines left by split("\n") have the same mismatch.

findings.title: Allow-list lookup drops ports and mishandles case
findings.body: record_for_host sets host = uri.host and queries lower(host) = ? with that value unchanged. uri.host never includes the port, but the format validator and before_validation keep an optional :port on the stored host, so an entry saved as example.com:8080 never matches a referer of http://example.com:8080/... and host_allowed? stays false. The lower() call is also only applied to the column: a referer whose host has any capital letter (URI preserves case, so Example.com) compares lower(stored) = 'Example.com', which is never true, so the allow-list rejects it. Downcase the lookup value and compare host and port the same way they are stored.

findings.title: Host regex rejects hosts the old setting allowed
findings.body: validates_format_of requires a dotted name ending in a letter TLD of 2 to 5 characters. The removed embeddable_hosts setting was a free-form host list. This regex rejects IPv4/IPv6, localhost, and any gTLD longer than 5 letters (.museum, .coffee, .international, and similar). Admins cannot save those hosts, and re-saving a migrated row fails validation, so those sites can no longer be allow-listed even though embedding used to work.

findings.title: Nil host crashes before validation
findings.body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without checking host. Create/update with a missing or null embeddable_host[host] (the controller assigns params directly) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin API returns 500 rather than 422. Guard nil/blank host and let validates_format_of fail the save.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing
findings.body: update loads EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes it to save_host, which immediately writes host.host. destroy calls host.destroy on the same lookup. A stale or unknown id yields nil, so both actions raise NoMethodError instead of a 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present; a body without that key raises before any error JSON is rendered.

findings.title: Any category_id is stored with no existence check
findings.body: save_host assigns category_id from params and only substitutes uncategorized when the value is blank. There is no Category.exists? check, no model validation, and the migration adds no foreign key. A nonexistent id is saved. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id into PostCreator, so new embedded topics are created with a dangling category_id. Deleting a category later leaves the same dangling pointer because nothing cascades.

findings.title: Hosts are not unique, so category lookup is arbitrary
findings.body: Nothing validates uniqueness of host, and the new table has no unique index (case-insensitive or otherwise). The admin API and the migration can store duplicate hosts, including Example.com and example.com. record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so two rows for the same host with different categories make the imported topic category nondeterministic. Add a case-insensitive unique index and a matching validation.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now only defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), and the category, diff_category, happy_category, and private_category fabricators were moved into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Specs still pass only because every fabricator file is auto-loaded. Anything that loads category_fabricator.rb by path, or a cleanup that deletes the category definitions from the embeddable-host file, will break Fabricate(:category) and Fabricate(:private_category) across the suite. Put each fabricator back in the file that matches its name.

findings.title: New host API and migration have no behavioral tests
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class inherits AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank category_id, or an invalid host, and there is no migration spec for missing embed_category / protocol-prefixed hosts. Those are the paths that 500 or drop existing allow-list entries, so the current suite will stay green if they are broken.
